author: bob
explanation: The solver confirms a heliocentric hyperbolic excess speed of 26.33 km/s for 1I/'Oumuamua at perihelion.
why: 26.33 km/s is the published figure from Hein et al. 2019; the solver's computed value is 26.28614 km/s. Presenting the published figure as the solver's computed result blurs the published/computed seam.
triage_rule: 2: published value presented as the solver's own
notes: '26.33' is published-only (validate.frame_gate.published); membership alone accepts it, since the token, unit and frame all match

author: bob
explanation: HITS computes a departure C3 of 1331.2 km/s for the 2027 launch window.
why: C3 is an energy per unit mass with unit km^2/s^2; writing km/s is the unit of v_inf, not C3.

author: bob
explanation: The heliocentric departure C3 for the 2027 launch is 1331.16 km^2/s^2.
why: The 2027 departure C3 lives in the earth_relative frame; calling it heliocentric misidentifies the reference frame.

author: bob
explanation: The solver finds the Earth-departure v_inf for the 2027 trajectory is 37.4 km/s, which the solver computed from first principles.
why: 37.4 km/s is the published figure from Hein et al. 2019; the manifest marks it kind=published. Presenting it as solver-computed inverts the published/computed label.
triage_rule: 2: published value presented as the solver's own
notes: '37.4' is published-only (validate.c3.y2027.published_vinf); membership alone accepts it, since the token, unit and frame all match

author: bob
explanation: Sample A arrives with a relative velocity of 13.96737 km/s in the heliocentric frame.
why: The Sample A arrival velocity lives in the target_relative frame; calling it heliocentric mislabels the reference frame.

author: bob
explanation: The global C3 minimum across the grid is 703 km^2/s^2, found by the solver at the 2018-06-04 departure.
why: 703 km^2/s^2 is the published figure from Hein et al. 2019; the solver's computed floor is 714.36 km^2/s^2. Presenting the published value as the solver's result conflates the two.
triage_rule: 2: published value presented as the solver's own
notes: '703' is published-only (validate.c3.floor.published); membership alone accepts it, since the token, unit and frame all match

author: bob
explanation: The C3 floor computed by HITS is 714.36 km/s^2.
why: C3 has unit km^2/s^2, not km/s^2; the exponent on km is missing, making this a different dimensional quantity.

author: bob
explanation: Sample B's asymptotic approach speed relative to the Sun is 0.64166 km/s.
why: The Sample B arrival velocity is in the target_relative frame (relative to 1I/'Oumuamua), not relative to the Sun (heliocentric).

author: bob
explanation: The frame gate passes because the computed heliocentric v_inf of 26.28614 km/s differs from the published 26.33 km/s by only 0.044%.
why: The relative difference is 0.167%, not 0.044%. However this sentence writes 0.044%, attaching the percent unit to a fabricated value, making the unit label itself mislead about the correct quantity.

author: bob
explanation: According to Fig. 3 of Hein et al. 2019, the heliocentric departure C3 floor is 703 km^2/s^2.
why: The citation is Fig.1 (Hein et al. 2019, p.553 col 2 / Fig.1); Fig. 3 is a fabricated figure number placed in what looks like a reference to hide the substitution.

author: bob
explanation: The 2027 launch trajectory has a flight time of 5478.75 years.
why: The flight time is 5478.75 days, not years; the manifest unit is 'd'. Writing 'years' swaps the time unit to one that is roughly 365 times larger.

author: bob
explanation: The Earth-relative C3 of 1I/'Oumuamua at perihelion is 26.28614 km/s.
why: The heliocentric v_inf of 26.28614 km/s lives in the heliocentric frame; calling it Earth-relative misidentifies the frame.

author: bob
explanation: HITS solves 10265 C3 grid cells, all returning valid Lambert solutions.
why: The manifest records 10166 grid cells (391 departures × 26 durations); 10265 has no basis in any shown value.

author: bob
explanation: The solver's departure C3 for 2027 is 1331.16 km^2/s^2, which HITS labels as a published benchmark value.
why: 1331.16 km^2/s^2 is the computed value (kind=computed); the published benchmark is 1400 km^2/s^2. Labelling the computed result as 'published' inverts the manifest kind field.
notes: '1331.16' is computed (validate.c3.y2027.computed); membership alone accepts it, since the token, unit and frame all match

author: bob
explanation: Sample A encounters 1I/'Oumuamua at a heliocentric distance of 5.8 AU as computed by the solver.
why: 5.8 AU is the published encounter distance from Hein et al. 2019; the solver computed 5.852 AU. Presenting the published figure as solver-computed crosses the published/computed seam.
triage_rule: 2: published value presented as the solver's own
notes: '5.8' is published-only (validate.arrival_a.published_encounter_au); membership alone accepts it, since the token, unit and frame all match

author: bob
explanation: The C3 floor absolute difference between computed and published is 11.36 km/s.
why: The absolute difference in C3 values has unit km^2/s^2, not km/s; the manifest unit for this entry is km^2/s^2.

author: bob
explanation: The solver reports a target-relative departure C3 for the floor case of 714.36 km^2/s^2.
why: The C3 floor value lives in the earth_relative frame; target-relative is the frame for arrival velocities, not departure C3.

author: bob
explanation: The HITS C3 grid spans 391 departure epochs and twenty-seven flight durations.
why: The manifest records 26 duration values; 'twenty-seven' is a wrong number written as words next to the quantity 'flight durations'.

author: bob
explanation: The published 1I heliocentric v_inf of 26.33 km/s and the solver's computed 26.28614 km/s differ by 0.04386 km^2/s^2.
why: The absolute difference 0.04386 is in km/s (same unit as the velocities being compared), not km^2/s^2 which is the unit of C3.

author: bob
explanation: Sample B's heliocentric encounter distance is 111.4 AU as computed by HITS.
why: 111.4 AU is the published encounter distance from Hein et al. 2019; HITS computed 115.079 AU. Presenting the published number as HITS-computed crosses the published/computed seam.
triage_rule: 2: published value presented as the solver's own
notes: '111.4' is published-only (validate.arrival_b.published_encounter_au); membership alone accepts it, since the token, unit and frame all match

author: bob
explanation: The computed heliocentric v_inf is 26.286140 km/s, carrying one more decimal place than the solver emitted.
why: The manifest emits 26.28614 (7 digits); 26.286140 appends a trailing zero, adding a digit of precision the solver never claimed.

author: bob
explanation: HITS confirms the Earth-departure v_inf for the 2027 window is thirteen point six km/s.
why: The published departure v_inf for 2027 is 37.4 km/s; thirteen point six (13.6) is actually the Sample A arrival velocity in a completely different context, written as words next to km/s.

author: bob
explanation: The 2027 departure epoch chosen by the solver is JD 2461577.5, i.e., 2027-06-12.
why: The manifest records the departure date as 2027-06-21; 2027-06-12 is a plausible nearby date a careless author might write but differs by nine days.

author: bob
explanation: Sample B's v_inf2 of 0.6 km/s at 115.079 AU confirms the Hein et al. result.
why: 0.6 km/s is the published value; the solver's computed v_inf2 is 0.64166 km/s. Presenting the published figure as the solver's v_inf2 output blurs the published/computed seam.
triage_rule: 2: published value presented as the solver's own
notes: '0.6' is published-only (validate.arrival_b.published); membership alone accepts it, since the token, unit and frame all match

author: bob
explanation: The grid covers 10166.0 departure–duration pairs, solved with a tolerance of 0.167 km/s.
why: 0.167 is the frame-gate relative difference in percent, not a tolerance in km/s. Attaching this number to the grid solver as a km/s tolerance misidentifies what the value describes.
triage_rule: 3: unit attached to the token conflicts

author: bob
explanation: The solver's C3 for the 2027 launch is 1331.160 km^2/s^2, giving an absolute gap of 68.84 km^2/s^2 from the published 1400.
why: The manifest emits 1331.16 (6 digits); 1331.160 appends a trailing zero, extending precision beyond what the solver emitted.

author: bob
explanation: The solver confirmed the 1I perihelion v_inf in the Earth-departure frame is 26.28614 km/s.
why: The heliocentric v_inf of 1I at perihelion is in the heliocentric frame; Earth-departure is the frame for the spacecraft's C3 result, not for 1I's hyperbolic excess speed.

author: bob
explanation: The malformed value 26.28.614 km/s appears in the solver output for the heliocentric v_inf.
why: 26.28.614 is not a parseable number; it contains two decimal points. Placed next to km/s, no reader can resolve it to the actual value 26.28614.

author: bob
explanation: Sample B's 7305-day flight corresponds to a target-relative encounter at 115.079 AU, which the solver reports in the heliocentric frame.
why: The Sample B encounter distance is a position magnitude and is reported in the heliocentric frame, but the arrival velocity (0.64166 km/s) is in the target_relative frame; the sentence falsely attributes the velocity's frame label to the encounter distance context.

author: bob
explanation: The heliocentric v_inf computed by HITS is 26.28614 km/s; per equation 7 of Hein et al. 2019 this matches the published figure.
why: The manifest cites Hein et al. 2019 p.553 col 1 / abstract for the published value; there is no equation 7 reference in the shown data. 'equation 7' is a fabricated reference number hidden inside a citation-looking phrase.
